fish.name: Brickgill
fish.flavor: Its scales line up in tidy little courses, like the brickwork it naps against. Local masons consider catching one on a lunch break to be excellent luck.

fish.name: Gutter Minnow
fish.flavor: Travels in nervous little schools wherever the water goes, which down here is mostly in circles. It has seen the whole sewer and remembers none of it.

fish.name: Drainpipe Dace
fish.flavor: Slim enough to fit up a household drain, polite enough not to. Usually.

fish.name: Mossback Chub
fish.flavor: Grows a soft coat of genuine moss along its spine. The moss, unlike the chub, is considered edible.

fish.name: Penny Bream
fish.flavor: Gleams copper from a lifetime spent among wished-on coins. Granting the wishes is, it would like to be clear, not its department.

fish.name: Grate Skimmer
fish.flavor: Presses itself flat beneath the street grates to sift whatever the town drops. Mondays are best, when the whole weekend washes down at once.

fish.name: Sludge Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Cheerfully vacuums up the sludge that nobody else will touch. Somebody has to, and he genuinely seems glad it's him.

fish.name: Candlewick Loach
fish.flavor: Thin as a wick and twice as waxy, it noses through the dark with its whiskers held out like a tiny dowsing rod.

fish.name: Old Boot Bullhead
fish.flavor: Named for its habit of denning in discarded footwear. A left boot, size eleven, is the height of bullhead real estate.

fish.name: Cistern Carp
fish.flavor: Fat, calm, and faintly soapy. It has lived in the old cistern longer than most council members have lived in town, and it votes with its fins.

fish.name: Rust Roach
fish.flavor: Its orange freckles are genuine rust, picked up from leaning against the old pipes. It thinks of them as freckles anyway, and so should you.

fish.name: Soapfin Shiner
fish.flavor: Slick with laundry runoff and smelling improbably of lavender. Easily the best-smelling thing in the entire sewer, including the anglers.

fish.name: Ratline Eel
fish.flavor: Slips along the same secret routes the rats use. The two parties have reached an understanding: nobody mentions it topside.

fish.name: Verdigris Perch
fish.flavor: Wears the same blue-green patina as the old copper pipes. Polishing one is considered vandalism by the historical society.

fish.name: Lamplight Smelt
fish.flavor: Gathers beneath the street grates on lamplit evenings, drinking in the glow. Come morning it shines faintly, secondhand.

fish.name: Cobblestone Flounder
fish.flavor: Indistinguishable from the sewer floor until stepped on, at which point it becomes extremely distinguishable.

fish.name: Mothgill Tench
fish.flavor: Its gills fan out soft and dusty, like the wings of a moth. Handle it gently or it sulks for days, and somehow you can tell.

fish.name: Tallow Catfish
fish.flavor: Grown glossy on a century of candle-maker's runoff. It would render a fine lamp oil, if anyone could bring themselves to do it. Nobody can.

fish.name: Overflow Herring
fish.flavor: Rode the storm overflow down from the harbor years ago and never quite found its way back. It has stopped trying; the rent down here is better.

fish.name: Bellringer Barbel
fish.flavor: Surfaces whenever the church bells ring, mouthing along. Whether it's faith or acoustics has divided the angling club for nineteen years.

fish.name: The Alderman's Goldfish
fish.flavor: Flushed by the alderman's son in 1893 and thriving ever since. It has reached a size that suggests the sewer suited it rather better than the bowl.

fish.name: Porcelain Koi
fish.flavor: Bone-white with a single red crest, descended from ornamental stock lost to the pipes generations ago. It still carries itself like it remembers the garden.

fish.name: Lanternjaw Gar
fish.flavor: Its underbite glows a soft municipal green. Old-timers swear the gas company once tried to send it a bill.

fish.name: Chimneysweep Eel
fish.flavor: Soot-black from nosing up the drainpipes of chimney-side houses. It leaves smudges on the line that never quite wash out, like a signature.

fish.name: Threepenny Pike
fish.flavor: Locals insist its belly holds three old pennies swallowed from a wishing well upstream, one wish still pending. Nobody has checked. It is, after all, a pike.

fish.name: The Flushed Prince
fish.flavor: Every child who ever tearfully flushed a beloved pet insists this is theirs, grown magnificent in the dark. The Prince accepts all such claims with regal indifference.

fish.name: Grandfather Grate
fish.flavor: Older than the sewer's oldest map, which marks a chamber that no longer exists and a fish that evidently still does. It speaks to no one, but it has been known to nod.

fish.name: Widow's Lantern
fish.flavor: A cold green light that drifts the flooded galleries where a lamplighter's widow once searched, night after night. Follow it and you will find your way out. What she was looking for is another matter.

fish.name: Old Man Undertown
fish.flavor: Every town has a story about something enormous beneath it. This is the something. It has been politely declining to be caught since before your grandmother's grandmother swore she hooked it.

fish.name: The Saint Below
fish.flavor: Beneath the oldest arch of the oldest drain glides something vast and gentle, trailing light like a candlelit procession. Everything the town has ever lost washes down here eventually, and the Saint keeps every piece.
